title: AI in My Workflow | Christian Sanchez
description: How Christian Sanchez, a digital marketer, uses AI across localization, editorial planning, video, repurposing, GEO and AEO, and the tools he builds with Claude Code.

hero.title: AI in My Workflow
hero.subtitle: Localization, editorial planning, video, repurposing, GEO and AEO, and the tools I build with Claude Code

lede: I'm a digital marketer, and AI is part of how I work every day. I use it for the slow, repetitive parts so I have more time for the ideas, and I check everything it makes before it goes out. These are the places it shows up, from posts localized for 10+ regions to apps I built for myself.

p: At Cohesity I built an AI agent with Claude Code, loaded it with our style guide and brand guidelines, and built a localization feature into the Champions Hub. Employees could localize one post as they shared it to LinkedIn, or switch on the whole feed and browse every post in their own language and region, graphics included.

The agent adapted the region as much as the language: less US-centric, with the tone set for each place. Its versions came out about 99% ready. I reviewed them with my team and select Champion Advocates, and every fix went back to the agent so it learned.

blocks.h: From Calendar to Do's and Don'ts
p: At QAD Redzone and Cohesity I used AI across the editorial workflow: building the content calendar in Monday.com, writing briefs and first drafts that I then edited, setting up A/B tests, localizing content, and turning our guidelines into do's and don'ts docs the whole team could follow.
blocks.note: An illustration of the workflow. The rows are examples.
dos: Lead with the person, then the product

p: The Mars Men PSA was a project for a job interview. I had six takes: two hooks, three body takes and a call to action. AI transcribed every take, so I could read the shoot instead of scrubbing through it, and it helped me pick the hook. Then I cut the video by editing the transcript, and AI made the captions for sound-off viewing.
The short hook won. The "You weren't built to be average" take moved up to sit right behind it, and lines that repeated a point came out.
blocks.note: Recut for this page from the raw takes, with captions set behind the speaker. The transcript is from the real takes, and the playhead and highlighted line follow the video.

lines.t: Forget all the biohacking trends. You don't need another cold plunge, red light therapy, or magic mushroom coffee.
Low testosterone isn't about seed oils or your sleep tracker, and it's definitely not your underwear.
Most guys are blaming everything but the problem.
The truth? Most men today are running from the real work.
We're out of alignment, stuck in jobs we hate, scrolling our lives away, and wondering why our energy and drive are gone.
You weren't built to be average. You're not here to be tired, soft, or overlooked. You're built to stand out,
to lead, to walk into any room and command respect. Nailed it.
Stop chasing hacks and dodging your own potential. When you fix your foundation, your hormones, your habits, your mindset, everything else falls into place.
You want to feel like a man again?
Start living like one. Own your routine. Own your health. Own your results.
Push yourself. Get aligned with your purpose. You're not broken, okay?
You're just not living up to the standard you were made for. Let's get after it.

blocks.h: Written for Search Engines and AI Answers
p: People type keywords into Google. They ask ChatGPT a question. GEO and AEO, generative and answer engine optimization, mean writing for both.

At QAD Redzone in 2024 I organized our FAQs and blogs so search engines and AI answers could find them. At Nike I wrote alt text and product tags for both kinds of search: for someone who knows exactly what they want, and for someone who only knows roughly.
